cells.tense: You are in the middle of the work and the aim is steady in your hands.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are keeping steady, and what holding it costs the people around you — say both out loud to someone today.
cells.core:
You move at what you want and you move at it evenly. No lurching, no white-knuckle — the aim holds through the ordinary resistance of a week, and things you set in motion stay in motion because you kept your hand on them. You probably don't count that as work, but it is.

What tends to fall out of a grip that steady is the exchange. You can keep something so well that nobody gets to add to it or take from it. Give one thing away and let one thing come back — not as a test of whether it holds, just as the ordinary traffic of being among people. Keep that traffic open and the thing you're steadying stays worth steadying.
cells.sheetLine: Your aim holds. Let what you're holding move between people.
cells.verb: holding what the change produced, in a form that keeps
cells.place: on the line between wanting a thing and moving at it

cells.tense: You are bracing for a moment that has not arrived and may never be yours to meet.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you keep checking on this week and leave it alone for a whole day, without asking anyone whether it's still fine.
cells.core:
Keeping it safe has stopped being rest and started being watch. You're guarding a shape you already finished against futures that haven't happened — running the next bad morning, the next person who might undo it, the version where it all comes apart. Each check feels like protection. Mostly it just keeps you braced.

Nothing you're protecting is moving right now, and a thing held that tight stops being a thing people can touch. Step back far enough to see the shape whole instead of patrolling its edges. Let one person stand near the edge of it without your hand on them. Keeping a thing gets lighter when you're not also keeping the future.

cells.tense: You are at a door you walked through and have not left behind you.
cells.ask: Decide one small direction today — what you're moving at for the next few days — and tell someone who'll ask you about it tomorrow.
cells.core:
You know how to keep a stable shape, but nothing is aimed. There's a thing you finished or left behind and you're still near it, telling yourself you're weighing options when the weighing is the standing. So the days go by without a direction in them, and the even hand sits unused.

It doesn't have to be a big direction to count. Pick one thing worth moving at and start walking at it before the case is fully made — the case gets made by moving. Watch what feels like yours as you go, not what sounds right from the chair. Direction comes back on its own once there's something in front of you again.
cells.sheetLine: You're steady and going nowhere. Pick one thing to move at.

cells.tense: You are anchored to something already and you talk about it like drift.
cells.ask: Write down three things you will not move on this month, and say one of them to someone before the day ends.
cells.core:
People close to you can feel what you keep to — the thing that doesn't move no matter what the week does, the shape you keep and don't talk about. You call it keeping your head down, or getting through it. That grip is already picking what you do next.

Unsaid, it just looks like where you happen to be standing. A keep you name becomes a stance: other people can work with it, and so can you. There's a plainness under this that doesn't need announcing — a thing you stand on, and it isn't a case you make, it's just where you stand. Say what it is and it stops being furniture.
